- **Ask cards:** the Ask card button is now "Add to sprint".
- **The ribbon:** its New Story button adds to Next sprint too.
- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+Enter no longer sends a story. It now moves the focused story between Next sprint and the Backlog. That choice is mine.
- **While paused:** the pause now only has to block sending the sprint.

content.content:
## Stories

A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title, a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode, "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour, as the [PromptModes](../prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes) colours it; its title, in the body's text colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small icon for anything attached, and, once it has been sent, its status as a task's is shown. Hovering a row shows a menu button at its right. A story has no Send of its own, as the sprint says.
Clicking a row opens it beneath, expanded in place, the others moving down: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a [GrowingTextInput](../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input) with the chat input's highlighting, completions, and slicing, as the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) has, and its attachments beneath; and its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat input shows them. Every change is saved as it is made. Only one story is open at a time; Escape or clicking its row again closes it.

## Creating

Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of Next sprint, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a story at the end of Next sprint, open, its title focused, in the mode last picked for a story. However a story is added, it goes into Next sprint, at its end: a new story, a duplicate, an accepted proposal for a new story, and one added from an Ask answer's card alike. It can then be moved to the Backlog to wait, as the sprint says. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as its prompt.
A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), to break it into stories, each with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

## Sprint
## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.
69:Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
70:Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than the Backlog's heading.
84:Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into Next sprint, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Next sprint" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens it.
89:The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
90:Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.
95:The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

content.text:
Every way of adding a story now puts it at the end of Next sprint, and sending the sprint is the only way a story reaches work. The planning, sprint, ribbon and card tests pass in a scratch copy, including a new keyboard check that Ctrl+Enter only moves a story and never sends it. I haven't tried it in the running app.

- **New stories:** the "New story" line now sits only at the foot of Next sprint. It, Ctrl/Cmd+N and the ribbon's New Story all add a story at the end of Next sprint, with its title focused.
  - Pressing Enter on a title still starts the next story beneath it within Next sprint. From a Backlog story, the next one goes to the end of Next sprint instead.
- **Other ways in:** duplicates and accepted "New story" proposals also go to the end of Next sprint. An accepted proposal's note now reads "Added to Next sprint". Ask cards' "Add to sprint" already did this.
- **Ctrl+Enter:** moves the focused story between Next sprint and the Backlog. The "Move to…" menu items show the shortcut.
- **Empty-state text:** Next sprint and the Backlog now say how to fill them under these rules.

The per-story Send and the pause blocking only the sprint were already in place from the previous step.
